description: Run-owned cohost observations. One case/size/cohort at a time. Exact terminal CSV-derived gauges and approximate live rates are separate; offline replay uses original timestamps. No equal-HA, steady-state, device-durability or microsecond-hardware-latency claim.

panels.title: Scope, clocks and historical replay
panels.description: Read before comparing cases.

options.content:
### One case, one contract — not a pooled leaderboard
Select exactly one run and case. Case context below preserves requested backend, workload profile, cohort/contract, value bytes and repeat; payload backend identity may differ. Never compare five sizes or different durability/HA contracts as one population.

**Cohost observer:** capped collector shares the controller and root volume. Caps do not prove zero perturbation. This dashboard is neither equal-HA nor steady-state evidence. Raw latency CSV and admitted source/config/deployment receipts are authoritative; a batch latency is for the complete API group, not divided by its keys.

**Historical restore:** use the archive's original absolute time range; no live targets are contacted. No data / one-scrape short intervals are not zero. Terminal cards use the last real sample in this range, not a replayed current timestamp. Host rates use rolling windows and are not exact per-case device attribution.

API, response and scheduling are separate clocks, **not additive engine stages**. Successful latency is conditional on outcome=success. Grafana cannot invent microsecond hardware latency, pure wire RTT, device durability, or unavailable stage profiling.

panels.title: Case context and actual data availability
panels.description: State is exporter state, not successful outcome. Final=1 requires an actual final metrics snapshot; terminal status can be failed without numeric summaries. Context labels are retained even for a single scrape.

panels.title: Exact terminal goodput, offered and rejected rates
panels.description: Complete measurement rows only. Offered, success and rejected share the identical elapsed measurement duration; no rate() required. Failed/absent summary is No data, never zero. Keys/s and value MiB/s are separate units, not API call counts.

panels.title: Exact terminal offered, success, rejected and outcome counts
panels.description: All scheduled arrivals are offered calls. Success is only outcome=success; rejection/error/timeout/unknown are not success. Outcomes partition offered calls. Counts and timed samples may differ; missing clock samples are absent, not zero.

panels.title: Exact terminal api quantiles — outcome=$outcome
panels.description: Backend API dispatch through materialized response. Not pure network/device latency. Exact raw-sample per-operation quantiles from admitted measurement rows, not histogram interpolation. Conditional on selected outcome (default success); p99/p999 remain descriptive for small populations. quantile=1 is maximum. Never average quantile gauges.

panels.title: Exact terminal response quantiles — outcome=$outcome
panels.description: Scheduled arrival through completed response, including scheduling and API time. Not the sum of independent quantiles. Exact raw-sample per-operation quantiles from admitted measurement rows, not histogram interpolation. Conditional on selected outcome (default success); p99/p999 remain descriptive for small populations. quantile=1 is maximum. Never average quantile gauges.

panels.title: Exact terminal scheduling quantiles — outcome=$outcome
panels.description: Scheduled arrival through backend dispatch. Rejected or untimed populations can lack this clock. Exact raw-sample per-operation quantiles from admitted measurement rows, not histogram interpolation. Conditional on selected outcome (default success); p99/p999 remain descriptive for small populations. quantile=1 is maximum. Never average quantile gauges.

panels.title: Live rolling offered, success and rejected calls/s
panels.description: Rolling monotonic-counter rates, not exact terminal goodput. Requires at least two scrapes and changing producer snapshots; frozen final snapshots are not live traffic. No zero-fill. Operations stay distinct; measurement phase only.

panels.title: Live p95 bucket estimates — outcome=$outcome
panels.description: Approximate histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(bucket)), per selected case, operation and outcome only. Not exact CSV quantiles or hardware-stage latency. Missing/short/frozen intervals remain No data. No aggregation across cases, phases, operations, sizes or contracts.

panels.title: Scrape / kernel collector availability
panels.description: Historical target health, not benchmark success. Missing target/unsupported collector is No data, not up=0. Node health is shown over the selected case visibility interval. Host labels identify role and index.

panels.title: Host busy CPU fraction
panels.description: Per host non-idle CPU fraction averaged across its logical CPUs. Includes benchmark, OS and cohost observer. Rolling-window boundary overlap is possible; not cgroup CPU or isolated workload attribution.

panels.title: Host memory: available and total
panels.description: Kernel MemAvailable and MemTotal gauges; available is not free memory and includes reclaim estimates. Includes all workloads and observer.

panels.title: Host PSI stall fractions
panels.description: Kernel pressure seconds/s: waiting=some tasks stalled; stalled=all non-idle tasks stalled (full). Unsupported pressure files remain No data. Not sums of CPU/memory/IO service time.

panels.title: Host device disk read / write bytes/s
panels.description: Actual Linux device diskstats counters, not logical WAL bytes/RMA/cache reads. Default includes all observed devices; select a WAL device only with retained mapping evidence, never infer one by name. Partitions/stacked devices may double-count if summed; no host/device summation here.

panels.title: Host diskstats mean request time and average queue depth
panels.description: Mean read/write request time = diskstats time counter rate / completed request counter rate, only when completed rate > 0. Includes software queue effects, NOT microsecond hardware latency or a percentile. Weighted IO seconds/s is average outstanding requests, not latency; no zero denominator fallback.

panels.title: Host network receive / transmit
panels.description: Per observed non-loopback interface. Linux NIC counters are not logical RMA payload bytes, pure wire RTT or guaranteed fabric-hardware counters. Device disk selector deliberately does not filter NIC names.

panels.title: Explicit cgroup availability
panels.description: 1=readable explicitly selected cgroupv2, 0=unavailable; absent=no cgroup selection or no scrape. No arbitrary process scans. Unsupported individual kernel fields remain absent even if availability=1.

panels.title: Cgroup CPU consumption
panels.description: LIVE CPU usage seconds/s, where 1 is one fully busy logical CPU. Requires at least two scrape samples; one point is No data, never zero. Actual host/cgroup scrape interval is 5s. Not divided by a guessed core count or cap. Observer overhead remains uncalibrated. Terminal boundary deltas are shown separately below.

panels.title: Cgroup throttled time and period fraction
panels.description: LIVE throttled seconds/s and throttled periods / periods are different signals. Actual scrape interval is 5s; one-point series are No data, not proof of no throttling. No max-minus-min shortcut or zero-fill. Throttled seconds may exceed wall seconds with parallel scheduling. A zero/absent period-rate denominator gives No data. Validated terminal interval gauges are separate below.

panels.title: Cgroup current and lifetime peak memory
panels.description: Actual cgroup memory.current and memory.peak. Lifetime peak is not a per-case peak unless the selected cgroup was created for this case. Parent/child cgroups can overlap; never sum without ownership evidence.

panels.title: Cgroup device IO: bytes/s and operations/s
panels.description: LIVE io.stat rates require at least two samples at the actual 5s scrape interval; one-point series are No data, not zero IO. Explicit cgroups and major:minor device identities only. No WAL-device mapping is inferred. IO attribution is not physical media service or durability. Separate terminal interval gauges below need no rate inference.

panels.title: Cgroup OOM kills — rolling counter increase
panels.description: Counter increase over the rolling rate interval; Prometheus extrapolation may yield fractional estimates. No samples/short intervals are No data. Zero is valid only for an observed unchanged counter with sufficient scrape history.

panels.title: Logical native WAL bytes — not device IO
panels.description: Native wal_written_bytes is a GAUGE (never rate it). wal_written_bytes_type is a cumulative COUNTER; this last observed total is not a measurement-only delta. Includes adapter lifetime/preload/warmup. Logical owner WAL reads and RMA completions in the instrumentation panel are not device IOPS, physical reads or hardware latency.

panels.title: Observed instrumentation and ADAPTER-LIFETIME read paths
panels.description: Read-path GAUGES come only from admitted read-evidence.json. ADAPTER LIFETIME includes preload, warmup and post-workload qualification; NOT measurement-only counts, live rates, hit fractions, device IOPS or hardware latency. Components/partitions remain separate. Availability is observed; absent evidence stays No data. The legacy write-profile flag is configuration evidence only, not proof of collected stages. The TERMINAL sampled-prefix panel below requires real runtime-enabled write-diagnostics.json and observed samples; no fabricated serialization/WAL/NIC/replication timings.

panels.title: TERMINAL boundary accounting availability and elapsed seconds
panels.description: Controller-validated same-boot, same-cgroup-inode before/end accounting. The host-local monotonic interval includes driver/oracle, background work and gate/control-plane overlap; NOT pure operation CPU or measurement-only stage time. Availability 0 means rejected/unavailable; absent means no evidence. Elapsed seconds are observed boundary separation, NOT benchmark API exposure or a live rate interval. resource_host_index identifies the measured host, not exporter placement. Sampling and observer overhead remain uncalibrated.

panels.title: TERMINAL interval CPU seconds and throttling
panels.description: Validated boundary CPU/throttling seconds and observed period counts, NOT Prometheus rates. A throttled-period fraction can be computed only for a positive observed period delta; it is undefined at zero. Missing counters stay No data; validated zero deltas remain real zeros. Includes driver/oracle, background work and gate/control-plane overlap; not pure operation CPU, measurement-only stages or the benchmark API clock.

panels.title: TERMINAL interval IO bytes and boundary memory
panels.description: Observed IO byte deltas summed across all owned-cgroup devices (raw accounting frames retain device identities), plus end-boundary memory.current / cgroup-lifetime memory.peak gauges. Missing counters stay absent, not zero. Accounting includes driver/oracle/background/gate overlap; not physical media latency, durability or pure measured-operation IO. Memory peak is not a per-measurement maximum. Do not sum overlapping parent/child groups or turn these gauges into live rates.

panels.title: TERMINAL write stage totals — distinct scoped populations
panels.description: Real schema-1 write-diagnostics.json only. TWO INDEPENDENT POPULATIONS: scope=sampled_prefix is bounded owner/transport/native write samples; scope=measurement_boundary_cumulative_delta is the coordinator's FULL measurement-boundary counter window, including coordinator preparation/admission, storage wait, publication, checkpoints and prefix-blocked time. The coordinator window is not restricted to the sampled prefix, and its availability does not require owner samples. Never combine their counts or normalize one population by the other's samples. Accumulated ns clocks become seconds, NOT per-operation percentiles, pure network time or additive latency fractions. Nested/overlapping stages MUST NOT be added or drawn as a percentage pie. Prefix selection is not proven representative; clock/collection overhead is NOT zero. Absent/reset/unavailable intervals remain No data, with explicit availability=0 only when a recorded interval error exists. Inspect each population's clock_scope and the artifact's overlap_semantics.
